August 7, 2007 MAYOR CESAR SULIBlt Liliw, Laguna Dear Mayor Sulibit: This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion regarding the revocation of the appointment of an Office for Senior Citizen Affairs head where the grounds and the process of discharging an incumbent appointee are not specifically provided under RA No. 9257, its Implementing Rules and Regulations and other related laws. In reply thereto, may we invite your attention to Section 6 of RA 9257 which provides that: rng OFFICE FO' cmzEN AFFAIR' — nere 'hall be e.tabli$hed in all citiet and municipalltie$ an to headed by .en&r citisen be appointed by a term o' three O) yean reappointment from list three O) nominees the the bayan. The head the O'CA 'hall be ani.eed the City Welfare Deøel"ment by the Municipal Social Welfare Development "e VelGee Office. In view of the above-cited provision, it is clear that the term of office of the head of the Office for Senior Citizen Affairs is fixed by law, that is, for three years without reappointment. Well-settled is the rule in statutory construction that when the law speaks in clear and categorical language, there is no reason for interpretation or construction but only application.

In that regard, it bears to emphasize that once the law fixed the term of office, the holder thereof enjoys security of tenure. Such being the case no officer shall be removed sooner than the end of the term except for cause, as provided by law. Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUS(TÉkE A.
